---
title: "How to leave out the insertions the QC flags"
---

Some IBL insertions should not be used to train or evaluate a model: the probe is not where
its alignment places it, or a band of the recording is broken. `ephysatlas.qc` checks every
insertion of a feature release automatically and labels it per component. The labels ship
with the package as `ephysatlas.fixtures.pid_qc_filter`; reading them needs no account and
no data.

## The labels

Each insertion gets one label per component, `good`, `review` or `bad`:

| Component | Bad when |
|---|---|
| `alignment` | the recording is more typical somewhere else: deeper or shallower along the probe, sideways, on the track of another insertion, or swapped with another probe of the mouse |
| `lf` | the LF band is unusual for the brain regions the probe is in |
| `ap` | the AP band is unusual for those regions, or a fifth of the channels are dead or noisy |
| `waveform` | the AP band is bad, or the waveforms are unusual for those regions |

*Unusual for the brain regions* compares the recording with what the other insertions record
in the same regions, in MADs of each feature in each region, never with a model's prediction.
Only the data decide: no model, no auto-alignment and no manual label enters the QC.

```python
from ephysatlas.fixtures import pid_qc_filter

pid_qc_filter.VINTAGE, pid_qc_filter.LEVEL   # ('2026_W42', 'L3')
pid_qc_filter.qc_labels("16ad5eef-3fa6-4c75-9296-29bf40c5cfaa")
# {'alignment': 'good', 'lf': 'good', 'ap': 'bad', 'waveform': 'bad', 'checks': 'channels'}
```

`checks` lists the tests the insertion fails; their definitions are
`ephysatlas.qc.levels.TESTS`, `TRACK_TEST` and `FIXED_TESTS`. Unlisted insertions are good on every
component.

## Leave them out of a dataset

`excluded_pids` returns the insertions bad on any of the components you name:

```python
from ephysatlas.fixtures import pid_qc_filter

channel_bad = pid_qc_filter.excluded_pids()   # any component: 93 of 1,049 for 2026_W42
unit_bad = pid_qc_filter.excluded_pids(("alignment", "ap", "waveform"))   # 71
cautious = pid_qc_filter.excluded_pids(include_review=True)   # also those to review: 130
```

Pass the list as `exclude_pids` to the loaders:

```python
from ephysatlas.spatial_encoder.utils import LoadInsertionData

pids, features, xyz, planned_xyz = LoadInsertionData(
    VINTAGE="2026_W42", exclude_pids=pid_qc_filter.excluded_pids()
)
```

`alignment.ChannelDataset.load` and
`unit_level_encoder.prepare_data.prepare_latest_cells_encoder_data` take the same argument.

::: {.callout-note}
## The default

Without `exclude_pids`, the channel loaders leave out the insertions bad on any component,
`excluded_pids()`, and the unit loader those bad for their alignment, AP band or waveforms,
`excluded_pids(("alignment", "ap", "waveform"))`. The models released from `2026_W44` on are
trained this way; `ephysatlas.fixtures.misaligned_pids`, the hand-curated list of earlier
releases, is kept for reference only. An empty list keeps every insertion.
:::

## How an insertion is judged

A probe's channels are reduced to 100 µm depth bins. Each bin's region comes from its position, in
the finest parcellation that at least eight other insertions cover: the Allen regions (cortical
layers, hippocampal strata), else Beryl, else Cosmos. The reference of a region is the median and the MAD of what the
other insertions record there, so a bin's residual says how far it is from them, in MADs of that
feature in that region. The tests of position use one measure of fit: how well the recording follows,
along the probe, the profile expected from the regions it crosses (the correlation over the bins of
each feature, averaged over the features of a band and then over the bands). The tests come in three
groups:

| Group | Tests |
|---|---|
| Unusual for its regions | For the LF band, the AP band and the waveforms: the `level` of the band, and its `shape` along the probe, which ignores an offset over the whole probe |
| More typical elsewhere | The recording fits better up to 2 mm deeper or shallower (`depth`) or up to 1 mm sideways (`sideways`); it follows its own track no better than the tracks of the other insertions (`track`); or it and another probe of the mouse, at least 1 mm away, both fit better swapped (`swap`) |
| Dead or noisy channels | A fifth of the channels (`channels`) |

The band tests, `depth` and `sideways` become z-scores, `(x - median) / (1.4826 MAD)` over all the
insertions. The others have natural limits. `track` is a share of tracks: a typical recording fits
fewer than 3% of the other tracks as well as its own, and needs no calibration, because a track that
changes little along the probe fits no better than the others. `swap` is the sum of the gains of the
two probes, both positive, and a dead channel is dead.

## Levels

The QC has five nested levels of sensitivity: an insertion is bad when a band test is beyond 7, 6,
5, 4.5 or 4 (L1 to L5), `depth` or `sideways` beyond 5, 4, 3.5, 3 or 2.5, more than 90, 80, 65, 55 or
45% of the other tracks fit it as well as its own, or when `swap` or `channels` fails. The position
tests have their own limit because their z-scores have short tails. The fixture is written at
**L3**, which marks 9% of the 2026_W42 insertions; an insertion is *review* when it is bad only at
L4.

To see what a level catches, the same problems are planted in 150 random insertions. At L3, 9% of
those insertions are marked bad as recorded, and with a problem planted: 48% of those moved 1 mm
along the probe, 74% of those moved 2 mm, 37% of those moved 1 mm sideways, 45% and 38% of those with
their LF or AP band replaced, 54% and 36% with noise added to it. A 500 µm shift along the probe is
the hardest (20%): many insertions as recorded are displaced by a few hundred µm already.

To rebuild the filter, or write it at another level (the measurements are cached, and only
the last stage runs):

```bash
python scripts/build_pid_qc_filter.py --stages levels --level L3 --write-fixture
```

The first run measures every insertion of the release (minutes). It needs the release's
features only, and Alyx once for the mouse of each insertion; see the script's docstring.
